Conversely, the downside risks include unforeseen economic downturns, significant geopolitical events, widespread natural disasters, or unexpected regulatory changes that could severely impact the underlying system and cause the value to fall below the lower bounds. These types of "tail events" are difficult to quantify within standard models but represent scenarios that could drastically alter the trajectory.
